findings.title: KeyError when existing integration metadata has no "sender"
findings.body: The user-match check reads `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` directly. However, `build_integration` only writes `metadata["sender"]` when `state.get("sender")` is truthy, and none of the pipeline views bind `sender` (the happy-path test even asserts that the resulting metadata contains no `sender` key). This means integrations created by this very pipeline have no `sender` in metadata. Whenever such an ACTIVE integration exists without a remaining OrganizationIntegration (e.g. a re-install/re-link after the org integration row was removed, or an orphaned integration), this line raises `KeyError` and returns a 500 instead of the intended friendly failure page. It also means the new 'authenticated user == installer' protection can never apply to pipeline-created integrations. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and handle the missing case explicitly, and/or bind `state["sender"]` from the OAuth-authenticated user in the pipeline so `build_integration` records it.

findings.title: Uncaught exceptions from token exchange and get_user_info produce 500
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(...)` (line 423) and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) are not wrapped in error handling. Only `safe_urlread`/`parse_qsl` are guarded. Network failures/timeouts or a non-success response (which these helpers raise as exceptions, e.g. ApiError) will propagate and yield a 500 rather than the pipeline's friendly failure page. Since the PR explicitly promises a graceful failure when GitHub cannot produce an access token, these calls should be wrapped and routed through `error(...)`.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404/build_integration path
findings.body: `test_installation_not_found` stubs the installation info endpoint with a 404, but the second request sends `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which does not match the pipeline signature, so the request now fails at the new state check with 'Invalid installation request.' and never reaches `build_integration`. The previous assertion (`The GitHub installation could not be found.`) was replaced, so the `ApiError`-404 handling in `build_integration` has lost all coverage, and the test name is now misleading (it tests a state mismatch, not a missing installation). Add a separate test that reaches `build_integration` with a valid state and a 404 installation.

findings.title: No test for the missing/invalid access_token failure path
findings.body: The PR description lists 'GitHub could not generate correct access_token from the code (wrong or attempt of re-use of code)' as a required failure case, but no test covers the branch at line 431 where the token response contains no `access_token`. The new tests only exercise the happy path, state mismatch, and the user-mismatch path. Add a test that stubs the access_token endpoint to return no token (or an error body) and asserts the 'Invalid installation request.' failure page, since this is a stated security-relevant guarantee.
